# 3D Website Designs

Use this skill to create strong visual direction for 3D-forward websites that feel premium, tactile, and intentional.

## Workflow

1. Define the goal.
   - Identify the brand, audience, primary action, and emotional tone.
   - Ask whether the page is meant to sell, showcase, explain, or impress.

2. Choose the role of 3D.
   - Decorative hero object
   - Product showcase
   - Immersive scene
   - Interaction driver
   - Storytelling backdrop

3. Pick a visual lane.
   - Minimal studio
   - Futuristic chrome
   - Organic fluid
   - Editorial luxury
   - Playful collectible
   - Sci-fi interface

4. Shape the scene.
   - Decide the focal point, depth layers, camera angle, and negative space.
   - Keep the composition readable before adding detail.

5. Define motion.
   - Use camera drift, parallax, hover response, reveal timing, and scroll progression.
   - Prefer a few deliberate motions over constant movement.

6. Set the surface language.
   - Define lighting, materials, palette, typography, contrast, and texture.
   - Make sure the 3D treatment supports the message instead of competing with it.

7. Produce the output.
   - Give a concise concept summary.
   - Describe the 3D scene.
   - Specify color, materials, typography, and motion.
   - Include implementation notes only when they help the design intent.

## Decision Points

- If the page is conversion-first, keep the 3D layer restrained and make the call to action obvious.
- If the page is brand-first, lean harder into atmosphere, contrast, and cinematic pacing.
- If the audience is mobile-heavy, simplify geometry, reduce effects, and suggest a fallback version.
- If the direction is unclear, present 3 distinct visual routes and recommend one.

## Quality Checks

- The design has a clear focal point within the first screen.
- The 3D element feels purposeful, not decorative noise.
- Text remains readable against the scene.
- Motion is smooth, controlled, and not distracting.
- The concept is realistic to build within performance limits.
- The page still works if the 3D layer is simplified.

## Response Format

- Concept
- Visual direction
- 3D scene
- Motion language
- Color and materials
- Typography
- Accessibility and performance notes

## Example Prompts

- Design a cinematic 3D landing page for a premium headphone brand.
- Create three art directions for a futuristic SaaS homepage with subtle WebGL motion.
- Describe a luxury editorial website with a glass and chrome 3D hero scene.
- Turn this plain marketing page into an immersive 3D-first experience.
